Proposal for the Edition Infrastructure

Git-based work, publication and preservation strategy

The Albrecht Edition combines federalized working groups with long-term data management. The joint academy director takes over operation and succession across individual workplaces. The infrastructure carries scientific cooperation, review and the coordinated book and digital publication.

Area repos hold together technically related work; a standard repo combines schema, IDs and rules. TEI and scripts are located in Git, the common index in the registry database. Released snapshots connect both. Tested data packets are integrated with origin manifest. The complete work stories remain in protected backgrounds. The public repository arises from released data and leads its own publication history.

Binding practice, understandable introduction and reliable responsibility are part of the infrastructure. The joint Git manual is reviewed twice a year and in an event-related manner. The employee agreement regulates contributions, usage rights and the protection of work history. Git identifiers document technical processing; scientific responsibility remains stated in TEI and contribution proofs.

The edition preserves citing results and the protected history of creation as different objects. The scientific archive is responsible for taking over and regulated research approaches. Data, schemas, index, procedures and manual versions remain connected; a complete reconstruction is tested annually. Exports and comprehensible interfaces allow a carrier or tool change.

Versioned procedures and tests make the edition learningable. OCR and LLM procedures are tested in a controlled manner; editorially relevant acquisitions remain professionally responsible. Process analyses examine agreed questions about handovers and bottlenecks. Individual performance rankings and working time profiles are excluded. The application includes operation, introduction, maintenance of rules, review, rights consulting, migration and archive services as ongoing tasks.

Reasons and Evidence

1. Scientific needs and decision-making rights

Federated groups. Own professional responsibilities, common rules and regular integration. This requires a mandated joint editorial team. The editorial departments are responsible for readings and comments. The edition committee decides on common principles and model changes. Technical write rights do not replace a scientific mandate. Expert experts need a readable test bench and a comprehensible answer to their objections.

2. Operation and tested alternatives

Joint Academy Management. A joint academy management can organise operations and succession across individual workplaces. Funding, scope of service, access and exit must be made binding. The joint academy management is responsible for entrances, operation and handover. The university offers existing advice, an external service technical provision; both alternatives are tested at partner access, performance, cost development and exit.

3. Data responsibility and integration

Area repos plus common standards. Area repos hold together technically related work; a standard repo connects schema, IDs and rules. Version dependencies are recorded in the band manifest. TEI and scripts are maintained in Git; the common index in the registry database. Reproducible snapshots connect both. Each data type has exactly one crucial care location. For the XML path eXist-db is tested with TEI Publisher on a test corpus; BaseX is an alternative for XML queries and applications. Editorial needs, output and operation decide on the choice. Source repo, source commit, index snapshot, rule version and acceptance are documented in the import manifest. The origin remains internal verifiable without copying the private history into the publication.

4. Publishing production and public approval

The approval is unexplained. Public publication is not yet a confirmed next step. Clear contract, third-party material, jurisdiction and editorial approval. Publisher data package, digital copies, commentaries and publishing PDFs have separate copyright notices. The legal/publication office documents subject matter and conditions; the publisher receives the agreed production status. The public environment takes over exclusively released data and its own history. Historical artefacts and metadata belong to the release examination.

5. People and binding project practice

Samir and his representative maintain manuals, profiles and technical tests; the specialist editorials release professional rules. Eva ensures introduction, maintenance time and announcement. Personal pseudonymous Git identifiers are managed separately. Scientific names remain visible in TEI and contribution proofs. The participation and access directory also covers service providers, publishers, IT and expert opinions. Entry and role changes are released on the basis of appropriate agreements and tasks. Employee agreement, rights arrangement and data protection information form the framework; the manual regulates the daily implementation.

6. Learning methods and legacy data

New rules apply only to future volumes at first. Smaller direct conversion; differences between volumes must be explained and taken into account when using them across the board. New interfaces, OCR and LLM procedures are tested with representative cases, professional examination and return route. The rule change is tested, manual version and documented scope. Old data are traced in designated orders; old standard versions remain understandable.

7. Review and production quality

Joint review rules connect the band editors. Test bench, confidential back channel and decision on reassessment are defined. The manual assigns rule version and test bench. Feedback is in the protected review area. Corrections from the sentence return to the relevant inventory. Dependent index and web editions are re-derived and checked together. The reimport check H06 is a concrete example of this.

8. Maintaining results and process history

The restoration is unexamined. A manifesto mentions components, but proves neither their preservation nor a functioning reconstruction. The Academies Association separates publication and process packages to its scientific archive. The work history itself is worthy of scientific preservation. A later access to research is decided upon application, purpose and protection examination; the end of the project does not open the holdings automatically.

Openness and independence

Openness of results concerns released edition data, open methods documented models and procedures. Process transparency is made possible by preservation and controlled research access. Documented TEI/register exports, available transformations and reconstruction instructions enable system change. Neither open source nor export claim alone prove a functioning replacement operation.

10. Process control and limits

A new analysis will be introduced after years. Precise improvements are possible; employees and former participants will also be visible afterwards. Clear the scope, admissibility, participation and opposition prior to use. The employee agreement and a concrete analysis sheet limit question, data, access and report. Key figures will be developed professionally with the team. Individual rankings and reconstructed working hours are excluded. New purposes, services and deeper evaluations will be clarified again before their use.

11. Resources and institutional commitments

The application contains permanently financed work for scientific and technical editorial staff including representation, professional acceptance, training, profile/rule maintenance, IT operations, rights consulting, migration and archive acquisition. Eva presents the employment, performance and financing plan to the academic association for this purpose. Before binding, the scope, duration and responsible institutions are decided in this plan.

12. Evidence and revision

A test corpus with output sample, a complete volume structure, the role/right matrix, an audited publication package and the archive acquisition description accompany the application. The association reviews the strategy annually as well as in case of model, carrier and rights changes. New analysis purposes also require the planned participation procedure.
